title: A Relativistic Version of the Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber Model
relevance: Primary source for the flash-ontology relativistic collapse position; supplies the no-preferred-foliation claim and the broken-time-reversal symmetry claim used in READING.md parts 1-3.
limits: Read via ar5iv/exa extraction: abstract, Section 1 (introduction, symmetry list item iii), Section 2.1-2.2 (GRW recall). Sections 3-8 (model definition details, joint distributions, foliation picture, low-velocity limit, predictions, comparisons) not read; no proofs checked.
section_locator: Abstract; Section 1 Introduction (incl. Bell epigraph and symmetry list); Section 2.1-2.2
assumptions: N non-interacting distinguishable particles, multi-time Dirac wavefunction; flashes as primitive ontology; collapse rate 1/tau and width a as new constants; fixed curved or flat background.
conclusion: A Lorentz-invariant stochastic collapse model exists whose local beables are flashes; it is nonlocal and violates Bell's inequality without a preferred slicing; time-reversal invariance is broken while rotation, space/time translation, parity and gauge invariance hold.
proof_status: Author's claims; definitions and GRW recall verified in extraction; model-construction proofs in Sections 3-5 not checked.
open_questions: Interaction and particle creation excluded by construction
positive-energy subspace restriction (Section 3.7, unread)
whether a becoming relation defined from flashes fails (LC) on the GH category (our conjecture, not Tumulka's)

title: Matter Density and Relativistic Models of Wave Function Collapse
relevance: Primary source for the matter-density relativistic collapse position and the frame-conflict problem READING.md parts 1 and 4 cite.
limits: Read via arXiv abs page extraction: abstract and Sections I (Background) and II (Scope) substantially; remainder (Sections III-V, the law and its properties) not read.
section_locator: Abstract; Section I Background; Section II Scope
assumptions: Wavefunction collapse with a relativistic law; wavefunction associated with spacelike hypersurfaces (Aharonov-Albert style); matter density as basic variable.
conclusion: A covariant matter-density function can be defined from the wavefunction on the past light cone of each point so that different Lorentz frames no longer assign conflicting densities, with predictions agreeing with known experiment.
proof_status: Author claims; background history (Bloch, Hellwig-Kraus, Aharonov-Albert) verified in extraction; construction not checked.
open_questions: Coverage of interactions (Section III-V unread)

title: Lessons of Bell's Theorem: Nonlocality, yes; Action at a distance, not necessarily
relevance: Primary source for the Myrvold position (nonlocality without action at a distance; collapse vs deterministic contrast) used throughout READING.md; also the reading that produced the Bell 1990 local-causality definition used in part 2 A1.
limits: Read via PhilSci PDF extraction: title/contents, Introduction, Section 2 (incl. relativistic-spacetime definition), Section 5 (Bell and local causality, incl. Bell 1990 and 1987 quotes), Section 6.1, Section 7 (local beables for collapse theories, incl. Ghirardi criterion and past-light-cone mass density), start of Section 8 (Everett comment). Sections 3-4 (toy model details), 6.2ff, 8 body, 9-11, appendix, references not read.
version: PhilSci-Archive preprint 12382; chapter in Shan Gao and Mary Bell (eds.), Quantum Nonlocality and Reality - 50 Years of Bell's Theorem, Cambridge University Press; printed pages not checked
assumptions: Interventionist conception of causation, temporally asymmetric; relativistic spacetime defined via transitive temporal precedence; separability and local beables vocabulary.
conclusion: Violations of Bell inequalities force nonlocality in any theory reproducing QM probabilities; deterministic theories need a preferred foliation (causal structure at odds with relativity); stochastic collapse theories need not; past-light-cone mass density serves as local beable for relativistic collapse.
proof_status: Argumentative chapter; no formal proofs; toy-model claims in Sections 3-4 not verified.
open_questions: Body of Section 8 (Everett comment) unread
